Career lesson: Safe bench setup, prediction, and measurement
Foundational CETa knowledge: Voltage, current, resistance, power, polarity, reference, open/short circuit, and Week 1 safety boundaries.
Career prerequisite activation: Use only the Week 1 CETa electrical-quantity and safety foundation. No prior bench-equipment experience is assumed.
Career-owned new learning: Bench power supply, DMM modes/jacks, current limiting, pre-power inspection, first-power sequence, stop conditions, and hazard logging.
Later deepening/mastery: Creates the bench habits required for every later measurement, bring-up, troubleshooting, and lab task.

Career lesson: Use expected node values to troubleshoot instead of guessing
Foundational CETa knowledge: Series/parallel networks, KVL/KCL, dividers, expected node values, and reference-node reasoning.
Career prerequisite activation: Bring forward Week 1 safe measurement habits plus the Week 2 CETa network equations and expected-node reasoning.
Career-owned new learning: Expected-versus-actual troubleshooting, node tables, first hypotheses, divide-and-conquer test-point selection, and one-change-at-a-time discipline.
Later deepening/mastery: Prepares the learner to choose instruments and high-information measurements rather than probe randomly.

Career lesson: Measurement planning, probe discipline, and uncertainty
Foundational CETa knowledge: DMM/scope connection rules, waveform quantities, measurement units, and safe references.
Career prerequisite activation: Use Week 1 bench safety and the CETa measurement concepts already taught. No professional measurement-planning experience is assumed.
Career-owned new learning: Question-first instrument selection, DMM/bench-supply/scope onboarding, probe/reference discipline, loading/accuracy/resolution, reproducible evidence, and logic-analyzer boundaries.
Later deepening/mastery: Becomes the common measurement workflow for filters, semiconductors, digital buses, MCU bring-up, RF work, and automated test.

Career lesson: Turn time-domain measurements into filter and fault evidence
Foundational CETa knowledge: Capacitance, RC time behavior, frequency response, and filter fundamentals.
Career prerequisite activation: Use the Week 3 measurement workflow plus CETa RC/filter behavior. The learner should already know amplitude, period, frequency, and time constant.
Career-owned new learning: Turn time-domain observations into evidence about cutoff, charging/discharging, distortion, and fault location.
Later deepening/mastery: Builds the habit of predicting waveform shape before using a scope for diagnosis.

Career lesson: A complete troubleshooting loop under a practical gate
Foundational CETa knowledge: Cumulative DC/AC/component fundamentals needed for the first troubleshooting gate.
Career prerequisite activation: Use Weeks 1–4 safety, expected-value, and instrument-selection habits. No new tool should appear without explanation.
Career-owned new learning: A complete reproduce → predict → measure → isolate → repair → verify troubleshooting loop under a practical gate.
Later deepening/mastery: Establishes the troubleshooting model reused through the rest of the course.

Career lesson: Characterize a filter or resonant network like a technician
Foundational CETa knowledge: RLC/resonance/filter response and frequency-domain relationships.
Career prerequisite activation: Bring forward Week 3 measurement planning and Week 4 waveform/filter evidence.
Career-owned new learning: Characterization tables, sweep planning, resonant/filter comparison, tolerance reasoning, and technician reporting.
Later deepening/mastery: Prepares for transistor/op-amp signal chains and later spectrum work.

Career lesson: Read a datasheet and design a relay/inductive-load interface
Foundational CETa knowledge: Diodes, rectification, inductance, switching devices, and protection concepts.
Career prerequisite activation: Use CETa device behavior plus prior pre-power and measurement discipline. Datasheet reading is introduced explicitly before design use.
Career-owned new learning: Datasheet pin/rating extraction, relay/inductive-load interface planning, flyback protection, and evidence-based component selection.
Later deepening/mastery: Prepares protected transistor/MOSFET switching and regulator bring-up.

Career lesson: Design and diagnose a protected low-side switch
Foundational CETa knowledge: Transistor/MOSFET switching behavior, protection, power dissipation, and bias/control ideas.
Career prerequisite activation: Use Week 7 datasheet and inductive-load discipline plus CETa transistor/MOSFET fundamentals.
Career-owned new learning: Protected low-side switching, gate/base drive checks, flyback paths, dissipation estimates, and layered fault isolation.
Later deepening/mastery: Creates a reusable switching pattern for actuators and embedded interfaces.

Career lesson: Rail-by-rail bring-up and supply troubleshooting
Foundational CETa knowledge: Power-supply, regulation, ripple, grounding, and load concepts.
Career prerequisite activation: Use Week 1 current-limited first power, Week 2 expected nodes, and Week 3 question-first measurement.
Career-owned new learning: Rail-by-rail bring-up, current signature interpretation, regulator checks, staged load connection, and supply-fault isolation.
Later deepening/mastery: Directly supports MCU board bring-up and project first power.

Career lesson: Measure and troubleshoot a signal chain
Foundational CETa knowledge: Amplifiers, signal conditioning, gain, bandwidth, loading, and clipping concepts.
Career prerequisite activation: Use Week 3 scope discipline and CETa amplifier/signal-chain models.
Career-owned new learning: Signal-path block reasoning, expected gain/offset/bandwidth, test-point planning, and stage-by-stage isolation.
Later deepening/mastery: Prepares mixed-signal and sensor-path diagnosis.

Career lesson: Real logic levels, pull resistors, debounce, and measurement
Foundational CETa knowledge: Digital logic levels, Boolean/state concepts, pull resistors, timing, and debounce.
Career prerequisite activation: Use the CETa digital logic model plus Week 3 measurement planning. No MCU register knowledge is assumed yet.
Career-owned new learning: Real logic thresholds, pull-up/pull-down behavior, switch bounce, scope/logic-analyzer evidence, and bit-mask preview only where CETa has prepared the binary model.
Later deepening/mastery: Prepares MCU GPIO, registers, interrupts, and serial-bus analysis.

Career lesson: Make physical changes traceable with Git and lab records
Foundational CETa knowledge: Soldering/rework/workmanship and physical interconnection concepts.
Career prerequisite activation: Use CETa workmanship/safety plus the established evidence rule. No version-control knowledge is assumed.
Career-owned new learning: Physical-change traceability plus Git from zero: repository, working tree, status, diff, commit, history, branch/tag, and known-good baseline.
Later deepening/mastery: Git becomes infrastructure for C, STM32, projects, test scripts, and portfolio evidence after this week.

Career lesson: Troubleshoot with competing hypotheses and high-information tests
Foundational CETa knowledge: Schematics, components, datasheets, signal flow, and prior troubleshooting evidence.
Career prerequisite activation: Use the established troubleshooting loop, schematic/datasheet literacy, and Git/lab-record baseline.
Career-owned new learning: Competing hypotheses, discriminating tests, divide-and-conquer strategy, root-cause verification, and concise failure reporting.
Later deepening/mastery: This reasoning model becomes the debugging backbone for C, MCU, buses, and projects.

Career lesson: Write and debug small C programs methodically
Foundational CETa knowledge: Binary/hex, logic, computer/processor concepts, and the idea that source code is translated into executable machine instructions.
Career prerequisite activation: No C programming is assumed. Use only CETa binary/computer fundamentals and Week 12 project-file/Git habits.
Career-owned new learning: A real C foundation: source/build model, variables/types, expressions, conditionals, loops, functions, arrays/strings/structs/enums, addresses/pointers, bitwise operations, warnings, and debugging.
Later deepening/mastery: Provides the programming prerequisites for embedded state/timing and STM32 work.

Career lesson: Responsive embedded architecture, volatile, and timing choices
Foundational CETa knowledge: Microprocessor architecture, registers, ports, binary/bit logic, clocks, and timing concepts.
Career prerequisite activation: Week 14 C must be usable before this lesson. Bring forward functions, types, arrays/pointers, bitwise masks, and debugging.
Career-owned new learning: MCU mental model, memory-mapped registers, read/modify/write, polling, blocking vs nonblocking, state machines, interrupts/ISR, shared state, volatile, and timing units.
Later deepening/mastery: Direct prerequisite for STM32 configuration, SWD debugging, GPIO, timers, and interfaces.

Career lesson: Create, flash, verify, and document a minimum STM32 bring-up
Foundational CETa knowledge: MCU architecture, GPIO/register concepts, clocks, and interface fundamentals available so far.
Career prerequisite activation: Use Week 14 C and Week 15 embedded architecture. No prior STM32 IDE, build, flash, or SWD experience is assumed.
Career-owned new learning: STM32 board/MCU identity, project/configuration, toolchain/build, output image, ST-LINK/debug probe, flash/reset/run, SWD, breakpoint, registers, GPIO proof, and fault layers.
Later deepening/mastery: Creates a known-good MCU baseline for host serial, I2C/SPI, sensors, and Project 1.

Career lesson: Build a robust Python serial client and evidence log
Foundational CETa knowledge: UART framing/levels and serial communication theory.
Career prerequisite activation: Use CETa UART theory, Week 14 programming ideas, and Week 16 known-good MCU baseline. No Python knowledge is assumed.
Career-owned new learning: Python from zero for test work, bytes versus text, modules/exceptions/files, pySerial configuration/read/write, message boundaries, parsing/validation, and evidence logging.
Later deepening/mastery: Python becomes the host/test foundation for later automated hardware validation.

Career lesson: Datasheet-to-wire integration and bus fault isolation
Foundational CETa knowledge: UART/I2C/SPI electrical and protocol models plus MCU peripheral concepts.
Career prerequisite activation: Use Week 16 STM32 bring-up, Week 17 host-side serial thinking, and CETa bus fundamentals. The learner should already understand what a register, pin, wire reference, and transaction are.
Career-owned new learning: One-interface-at-a-time datasheet-to-wire integration, transaction contracts, pull-ups/chip select, logic-analyzer setup, decoded evidence, and layered bus fault isolation.
Later deepening/mastery: Supports Project 1 peripheral integration and automated interface verification.

Career lesson: Terminate, inspect, continuity-test, and isolate a connection fault
Foundational CETa knowledge: Cabling, connectors, transmission media, continuity, and workmanship concepts.
Career prerequisite activation: Use CETa cable/media theory plus Week 3 measurement discipline and Week 12 workmanship evidence.
Career-owned new learning: Termination inspection, pin numbering/keying, strain relief, continuity/segment isolation, and serviceable harness documentation.
Later deepening/mastery: Prepares reliable project interconnects and employer-facing workmanship evidence.

Career lesson: Measurement procedure, spectrum interpretation, and technical handoff
Foundational CETa knowledge: RF/telecom fundamentals: frequency, spectra, modulation, transmission lines, and technician procedures.
Career prerequisite activation: Use CETa RF/telecom concepts plus Week 3 measurement planning. No spectrum-analyzer workflow is assumed.
Career-owned new learning: Spectrum-analyzer controls/settings, marker interpretation, measurement procedure writing, observation-versus-interpretation, and technical escalation/handoff.
Later deepening/mastery: Strengthens professional test procedure and handoff skills used in project validation.

Career lesson: Turn broad theory into rapid technician choices
Foundational CETa knowledge: Broad CETa theory accumulated across electrical, components, digital, communications, safety, and procedures.
Career prerequisite activation: Use all prior foundational models but continue to choose the smallest relevant model for each scenario.
Career-owned new learning: Rapid technician triage: identify the domain, select the likely evidence source/tool, state a hypothesis, and choose a safe next action.
Later deepening/mastery: Prepares requirements/project work where the learner must select methods without topic labels.

Career lesson: Write requirements and verification before building
Foundational CETa knowledge: Readiness review plus broad technical foundation.
Career prerequisite activation: Use the troubleshooting, documentation, Git, measurement, and interface habits already established.
Career-owned new learning: Requirements, acceptance criteria, verification methods, traceability, test planning, and scope control before build work.
Later deepening/mastery: Defines the contract for Project 1 and later automated validation.

Career lesson: Create a controlled project baseline before hardware bring-up
Foundational CETa knowledge: CETa readiness evidence and all prior technical foundations.
Career prerequisite activation: Requirements must exist before the project baseline. Git/project structure, lab records, and safety limits are already taught.
Career-owned new learning: Controlled project baseline: repository, configuration identity, issue/evidence structure, bench readiness, BOM/interface ownership, and reproducible start state.
Later deepening/mastery: Prevents first-power ambiguity and provides a known baseline for every Project 1 change.

Career lesson: Execute staged first power and establish a known-good baseline
Foundational CETa knowledge: Power, measurement, digital/MCU, safety, and component behavior.
Career prerequisite activation: Use the controlled baseline from Week 23 plus the Week 1/9/16 bring-up ladders.
Career-owned new learning: Project first power with inspection, continuity, current limiting, rail verification, reset/boot/debug checks, GPIO/UART proof, and baseline evidence.
Later deepening/mastery: Creates the known-good platform required before adding a sensor/peripheral.

Career lesson: Integrate one peripheral through a controlled vertical slice
Foundational CETa knowledge: I2C/SPI/interface theory, sensors, ADC/digital concepts, and prior measurement skills.
Career prerequisite activation: Use Week 18 one-interface workflow and Week 24 known-good project baseline.
Career-owned new learning: One controlled peripheral vertical slice from datasheet and wiring through firmware, capture, engineering-unit conversion, fault handling, and evidence.
Later deepening/mastery: Provides a stable functional slice that firmware architecture and automated test can exercise.

Career lesson: Separate drivers, application state, diagnostics, and recovery
Foundational CETa knowledge: MCU architecture, digital/state concepts, and the project peripheral now working.
Career prerequisite activation: Use Week 15 nonblocking/state/interrupt concepts and Week 25 working vertical slice.
Career-owned new learning: Firmware layering: drivers, application state, diagnostics, timeouts, error/recovery paths, versioned changes, and testable module boundaries.
Later deepening/mastery: Makes Project 1 observable and controllable enough for automated testing.

Career lesson: Design a maintainable automated hardware test
Foundational CETa knowledge: Measurement/test concepts plus the working Project 1 interface.
Career prerequisite activation: Use Week 17 Python/serial, Week 22 requirements/verification, and Week 26 observable firmware. No automated-test architecture is assumed beyond those pieces.
Career-owned new learning: Automated-test lifecycle, fixture/DUT boundaries, setup/stimulus/acquisition/evaluation/cleanup, PASS/FAIL/ERROR/INCONCLUSIVE semantics, configuration source-of-truth, logs, plots, and boundary tests.
Later deepening/mastery: Provides the evidence engine for deliberate fault injection and final reports.

Career lesson: Design controlled faults and write a defensible report
Foundational CETa knowledge: Broad electronics theory and established project/test baseline.
Career prerequisite activation: Use Week 13 root-cause reasoning, Week 22 verification design, and Week 27 automated evidence.
Career-owned new learning: Controlled fault injection, failure-mode coverage, evidence-preserving diagnosis, requirement/result traceability, corrective action, retest, and defensible report writing.
Later deepening/mastery: Produces the strongest troubleshooting story for the portfolio and interviews.

Career lesson: Assemble an employer-facing role-proof dossier
Foundational CETa knowledge: All practical electronics, measurement, workmanship, and troubleshooting foundations.
Career prerequisite activation: Only artifacts already created in labs/projects count as evidence; do not invent proficiency.
Career-owned new learning: Employer-facing role-proof dossier combining instruments, rework/harness quality, bring-up, troubleshooting, code, test evidence, and serviceability.
Later deepening/mastery: Feeds the application and interview package without requiring a new technical project.

Career lesson: Build an evidence-first application and interview package
Foundational CETa knowledge: Completed technical evidence plus readiness results.
Career prerequisite activation: Use verified project/lab evidence and accurate statements of personal contribution.
Career-owned new learning: Evidence-first portfolio, truthful resume bullets, 90-second transition story, technical project explanations, troubleshooting interviews, and job-description skill-gap analysis.
Later deepening/mastery: Creates a reusable application package and feedback baseline.

Career lesson: Run applications as an evidence-and-feedback loop
Foundational CETa knowledge: Course technical foundation is complete; remaining work is retention and targeted repair.
Career prerequisite activation: Use the existing portfolio/application package and real feedback. Do not restart mastered curriculum wholesale.
Career-owned new learning: Application/interview feedback loop, gap classification, targeted technical repair, portfolio maintenance, and bridge-role targeting.
Later deepening/mastery: Transitions Alfred from course delivery to ongoing targeted professional development.
